Research

Star–planet chemical connection

Volatile depletion and chemical fractionation

Volatile elements are depleted in planetary materials relative to their host stars. I quantify this devolatilization and model the physics behind it.

Publications

  • Volatile depletion in rocky planets as a chemical fingerprint of hybrid accretion
    H. S. Wang, A. Johansen, Z. Xu, M.-L. Steinmeyer, M. Lambrechts, E. van Kooten, C.-C. Yang, Z. Zhu, D. S. Lauretta, M. Bizzarro (2026)
    Nature Astronomy · DOI · arXiv
    Bayesian modelling of devolatilization during pebble accretion and collisional growth shows that the bulk silicate Earth needs a contribution of at least about 75% from two pebble-grown protoplanets, whereas bulk silicate Mars reflects 27 ± 5% pebble-accreted material and 73 ± 5% Vesta-like planetesimals.
  • A chemical perspective on planet formation in reduced systems
    U. Zaveri, H. S. Wang, P. A. Sossi (2026)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 709, A223 · DOI · arXiv
    Condensation sequences are not universal: in chemically reduced disks around stars with high C/O ratios, elemental ratios commonly treated as refractory may not reliably trace planetary bulk composition.
  • The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
    Y. Reinarz, L. Acuña-Aguirre, H. S. Wang (2026)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, accepted; arXiv:2611.12581 · arXiv
    Interior structure retrievals of 14 rocky exoplanets with two independent models find that 8 present an Earth-like devolatilization trend relative to their host stars, while only one shows a 1:1 relationship between planetary and stellar abundances.
  • Diversity of planetary origins and compositions traced by stellar abundance differences of co-natal star systems
    B. Bitsch, F. Liu, H. S. Wang (2026)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, accepted; arXiv:2610.32833 · arXiv
    Abundance differences between co-natal stars can be explained by the ingestion of planets whose compositions depend on where they formed, interior or exterior to the water and carbon evaporation fronts.
  • A Bayesian Search for Planet Engulfment Signatures in Solar Analogs
    Z. Cheng, S. X. Wang, F. Liu, H. Wang, Q. Sun, J. Buchner, M. Babatsikos, H. Chen, J. Zhang, Y.-S. Ting, Z. Guo, A. Dotter, S. M. Saad, J. Osses (2026)
    arXiv:2607.03504 · arXiv
    A Bayesian search of 113 solar twins and analogs identifies three candidates whose abundance patterns strongly favor planet engulfment, a nominal detection rate of 1–3%.
  • Oxygen and nitrogen isotopologs on cold COCONUTS-2b observed with MIRI/MRS
    H. Kühnle, E. C. Matthews, P. Mollière, P. Patapis, Z. Zhang, E. Nasedkin, D. Gasman, N. Whiteford, H. S. Wang, M. Ravet, G. Chauvin, M. Bonnefoy, D. Barrado, A. M. Glauser, S. P. Quanz (2026)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 710, A355 · DOI · arXiv
    JWST MIRI/MRS spectra of the cold planetary-mass companion COCONUTS-2b robustly detect three isotopologues (¹⁵NH₃, H₂¹⁸O and H₂¹⁷O), opening a way to trace formation through isotope ratios.
  • Chemical Abundances Shape History (CASH). I. A Link between Giant Planets’ Orbital Periods and Host Stellar C/O Ratios
    R. Zhang, J.-W. Xie, M. Pan, B. Liu, J.-L. Zhou, J. Wang, H. S. Wang, Y. Zhang (2026)
    The Astronomical Journal, 171, 302 · DOI · arXiv
    Stars with higher C/O ratios are more likely to host longer-period giant planets, a correlation supported by models of pebble-driven planet formation and migration.
  • Reconciliation of M Dwarf and FGK Stellar Abundances with Galactic Chemical Evolution
    T. C. L. Trueman, H. S. Wang, S. J. Mojzsis, D. Turrini, K. Heng, M. Pignatari (2026)
    The Astrophysical Journal, 1005, 205 · DOI
    M dwarf abundance trends align with those of FGK stars within uncertainties for most elements and agree well with Galactic chemical evolution predictions, resolving prior discrepancies.
  • Proto-planetary disk composition-dependent element volatility in the context of rocky planet formation
    R. J. Spaargaren, O. Herbort, H. S. Wang, S. J. Mojzsis, P. Sossi (2025)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 703, A218 · DOI · arXiv
    Element volatility depends on disk composition, and accounting for this predicts an even broader range of rocky planet compositions than previously considered.
  • Performance of the Stellar Abundances and atmospheric Parameters Pipeline adapted for M dwarfs-I. Atmospheric parameters from the spectroscopic module
    T. Olander, M. R. Gent, U. Heiter, O. Kochukhov, M. Bergemann, E. Magg, S. Cassisi, M. Kovalev, T. Morel, N. J. Miller, D. Souto, Y. Shan, B. Rojas-Ayala, E. Delgado-Mena, H. S. Wang (2025)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 696, A62 · DOI · arXiv
    Adapts the Stellar Abundances and atmospheric Parameters Pipeline of the PLATO consortium to M dwarfs and validates it on APOGEE spectra of 26 stars.
  • Towards characterising rocky worlds: Trends in chemical make-ups of M dwarfs versus GK dwarfs
    H. S. Wang, S. P. Quanz, S. Mahadevan, M. Deal (2024)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 688, A225 · DOI · arXiv
    M dwarfs and GK dwarfs follow significantly different [X/H]–[Fe/H] trends for most rock-forming elements, so scaling M dwarf abundances from Sun-like stars may bias constraints on their rocky planets.
  • Plausible constraints on the range of bulk terrestrial exoplanet compositions in the solar neighbourhood
    R. J. Spaargaren, H. S. Wang, S. J. Mojzsis, M. D. Ballmer, P. J. Tackley (2023)
    The Astrophysical Journal, 948, 53 · DOI · arXiv
    Devolatilized stellar abundances from the Hypatia and GALAH catalogues constrain the range of rocky exoplanet compositions in the solar neighbourhood, with metallic core sizes varying from 18 to 35 wt%.
  • Detailed chemical compositions of planet-hosting stars – I. Exploration of possible planet signatures
    F. Liu, D. Yong, M. Asplund, H. S. Wang, L. Spina, L. Acuña, J. Melendez, I. Ramirez (2020)
    Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 495, 3961–3973 · DOI · arXiv
    High-precision abundances of 16 planet-hosting stars show a variety of trends between abundance and condensation temperature, with no unambiguous chemical signature of planet formation.
  • The volatility trend of protosolar and terrestrial elemental abundances
    H. S. Wang, C. H. Lineweaver, T. R. Ireland (2019)
    Icarus, 328, 287–305 · DOI · arXiv
    Quantifies the Sun-to-Earth devolatilization pattern: Earth and the Sun share refractory composition but differ systematically in volatiles.
  • The elemental abundances (with uncertainties) of the most Earth-like planet
    H. S. Wang, C. H. Lineweaver, T. R. Ireland (2018)
    Icarus, 299, 460–474 · DOI · arXiv
    Provides concordance estimates, with uncertainties, of the elemental abundances of the bulk Earth, including a core mass fraction of 32.5 ± 0.3 wt%.
  • Chemical complementarity between the gas phase of the interstellar medium and the rocky material of our planetary system
    H. Wang, C. Lineweaver (2016)
    Proc. 15th Australian Space Research Conference, 15, 173–182 · arXiv
    Elements depleted in the gas phase of the interstellar medium are enriched in the rocky material of the Solar System, and vice versa.
